title: Relative insertion of one finite-poset vertex with a prescribed incoming slice arrow
statement:
Use universes, infinite regular cardinals and $\kappa$-filteredness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], nerves, quasicategories, full subcategories and coherent diagrams of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and joins and join slices of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. Small means in the fixed universe $\mathcal U$. Let $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ be an infinite regular cardinal, $A$ a finite partially ordered set, $B$ a small partially ordered set with $|B|<\kappa$, $\mathcal E$ a quasicategory in a containing universe, $\mathcal E_0\subseteq\mathcal E$ a full subcategory, and $F:N(A)\to\mathcal E$ a coherent diagram. Give $J=B\amalg\{\infty,\infty'\}$ its original order on $B$ and the relations $b<\infty<\infty'$ for all $b\in B$. Let $L\subset A$ be an order ideal and $a\in A\setminus L$ a minimal element of its complement. In the product poset $A\times J$ put
$$Q_L=(A\times(B\amalg\{\infty'\}))\cup(L\times\{\infty\}),\qquad Q_{L+a}=Q_L\cup\{(a,\infty)\},$$
with the induced orders. Suppose given $U:N(Q_L)\to\mathcal E$ restricting to $F$ on $A\times\{\infty'\}$ and taking all other vertices into $\mathcal E_0$. Set $R=\mathcal E_0\times_{\mathcal E}\mathcal E_{/F(a)}$, where the slice is the join slice: its $n$-simplices are maps $\Delta^n\star\Delta^0\to\mathcal E$ with final vertex $F(a)$ and initial face in $\mathcal E_0$. Assume $R$ is $\kappa$-filtered. Restriction of $U$ to the row $\{a\}\times(B\amalg\{\infty'\})$ defines $\rho_U:N(B)\to R$: an $n$-simplex is the image of the chain $(a,b_0)\leq\cdots\leq(a,b_n)<(a,\infty')$. For any poset $P$, write $P^{\triangleleft}=\{z\}\amalg P$ with $z<p$ for all $p\in P$, and $P^{\triangleright}=P\amalg\{\infty\}$ with $p<\infty$ for all $p\in P$. Suppose given $\beta:N(B^{\triangleleft})\to R$ with $\beta|_{N(B)}=\rho_U$, and write $d=\beta(z)$.

Then there exist $U':N(Q_{L+a})\to\mathcal E$ and $\beta':N((B^{\triangleright})^{\triangleleft})\to R$ such that $U'|_{N(Q_L)}=U$, $U'(a,\infty)\in\mathcal E_0$, $\beta'|_{N(B^{\triangleleft})}=\beta$, and $\beta'|_{N(B^{\triangleright})}=\rho_{U'}$. Here $\rho_{U'}$ is obtained from the row $\{a\}\times(B\amalg\{\infty,\infty'\})$ by the same final-vertex formula. Thus the edge $d\to\rho_{U'}(\infty)$ and all its triangles with $\beta(z\to b)$ are part of the specified coherent extension. These are equalities of simplicial maps on their entire boundaries. The case $B=\varnothing$ is included: $\beta$ is the vertex $d$ and $\beta'$ is an edge from $d$ to the new row object. No colimits, compactness or local-smallness hypothesis on $\mathcal E$ or $\mathcal E_0$ is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.15, proof (b), printed p.411 (PDF p.428), local relative version of the vertex insertion in proof (a). The source calls the comma argument a minor variation; this statement makes its distinguished-vertex extension precise. Read online; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Put $M=(A_{\leq a}\times B)\cup(A_{<a}\times\{\infty\})$ and $T=A_{\geq a}$. Minimality of $a$ in the complement of the order ideal gives $A_{<a}\subseteq L$. These are exactly the vertices strictly below and strictly above $(a,\infty)$, with the upper vertices indexed by $(t,\infty')$, $t\in T$. Every element of $M$ is below every such upper vertex. Thus $N(M)\star N(T)$ is a simplicial subset of $N(Q_L)$. Write $p=F|_{N(T)}$ and $S=\mathcal E_{0,/p}$. The definition of the join slice turns the restriction of $U$ to this join into $h:N(M)\to S$: on an $n$-simplex it is the restriction to its concatenation with $N(T)$. Its source lies in $\mathcal E_0$ because all lower vertices do, and $\mathcal E_0$ is full. Restriction to $a\in T$ gives $v:N(M)\to R$; on $C=\{a\}\times B$ it is precisely $\rho_U$, including every simplex.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.15(a), lower and upper links in the vertex induction; relative version for (b)

proof.text: Form the simplicial pushout $K=N(M)\amalg_{N(C)}N(B^{\triangleleft})$, identifying $C$ with $B$. The maps $v$ and $\beta$ agree on the identified subcomplex, so define $w:K\to R$. The canonical maps from both factors into $K$ are inclusions, since this pushout is computed degreewise along injections. The set of vertices of $M$ has cardinality at most $|A|(|B|+1)$. If $\kappa=\aleph_0$, $M$ is finite and a nondegenerate chain has bounded length, so $N(M)$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices. For uncountable regular $\kappa$, each finite-chain set has cardinality $<\kappa$, and their countable union still does. The same reasoning applies to $B^{\triangleleft}$. Every simplex of $K$ comes from one of the two factors, so $K$ is $\kappa$-small in the stated nondegenerate-simplex convention.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.15(b), explicit augmented lower-link diagram for the comma variation

proof.text: Apply the definition of $\kappa$-filteredness of $R$ to $w:K\to R$ to obtain a coherent cocone, hence a vertex of its fixed-diagram coherent cocone category $P_w$. The join-slice/cocone comparison gives a functor equivalence $J_w\to P_w$, where a vertex of $J_w$ is a map $K\star\Delta^0\to R$ restricting exactly to $w$. Apply a quasi-inverse to the cocone vertex to obtain $\bar w:K\star\Delta^0\to R$ with $\bar w|_K=w$; this boundary equality is part of membership in $J_w$. Denote its new final vertex by $y$. Restrict to $N(M)\star\{y\}$ to get $c:N(M)\star\Delta^0\to R$ with $c|_{N(M)}=v$. The other factor gives a map $N(B^{\triangleleft})\star\{y\}\to R$ extending $\beta$. Only a cocone is used; no colimit is required.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.15(a)-(b), filteredness on the augmented lower link; Proposition 4.2.1.5, printed p.241, converts the coherent cocone to a join extension with fixed boundary

proof.text: The poset $T=A_{\geq a}$ has least element $a$. The least-vertex slice-restriction theorem gives a trivial Kan fibration $r:S\to R$. Apply its stated relative lifting property with simplicial inclusion $N(M)\subseteq N(M)\star\Delta^0$, prescribed map $h:N(M)\to S$, and bottom map $c$. The equality $rh=v=c|_{N(M)}$ makes the lifting square commute. We obtain $H:N(M)\star\Delta^0\to S$ with $H|_{N(M)}=h$ and $rH=c$. Crucially the entire lower diagram is held fixed, not just the new cone vertex; therefore the already prescribed mixed simplices with every upper vertex are preserved.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.15(a), restriction along the least upper vertex; relative boundary lift needed for (b)

proof.text: Unpack the join-slice definition: $H$ is a map $(N(M)\star\{y\})\star N(T)\to\mathcal E$ restricting to $p$ on $N(T)$ and to the old $U$ on $N(M)\star N(T)$. The equality of these joins under reassociation follows directly from concatenating their three ordered blocks of vertices. Every chain newly added to $Q_L$ is uniquely a lower chain in $M$, then $(a,\infty)$, then an upper chain in $T$, allowing empty lower or upper blocks. Hence the new join and $N(Q_L)$ have intersection exactly $N(M)\star N(T)$ and union $N(Q_{L+a})$. Glue the two maps along their equal restrictions to define $U'$. Its new vertex is the source of $H(y)\in S$, hence lies in $\mathcal E_0$. Define $\beta'$ by restricting $\bar w$ to $N(B^{\triangleleft})\star\{y\}=N((B^{\triangleright})^{\triangleleft})$ (ordered $z<b<y$). It restricts to $\beta$ on the old left cone. On $N(B)\star\{y\}$ it is $c$; the equality $rH=c$ identifies this exactly with the final-vertex row map $\rho_{U'}$. All equalities hold degreewise, including degeneracies and higher triangles. When $B$ or $M$ is empty, the same joins allow empty blocks; in particular the restriction on $\{z,y\}$ is the required edge from $d$ to the new row object.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.15(b), explicit reconstruction of the relative extension from the lifted lower cone
